title: Loop host decides bounded acceptance
statement: Let $B$ and $F$ be Boolean finite Turing machines, let $a$ be a state of $B$, let $I$ be a predicate on pairs of Boolean words, $g$ a state-update function, $A$ a Boolean acceptance test, and $s_0$ an initial-word function. Let $R,T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Assume $F$ computes the binary digits of $R(|x|)$ on each input $x$ within time $T(|x|)$; $I(x,s_0(x))$ holds for every $x$ and is preserved by $g$; and for each $x$, the run of $B$ from its initial configuration reaches the seam configuration at state $a$ with tape words assigned by $s_0(x)$ within some time $t\le T(|x|)$, without having state $a$ at any earlier time. Also assume that for every $x,s$ with $I(x,s)$, there is a time $t$ with $0<t\le T(|x|)$ such that the run of $B$ from the seam configuration at $a$ with tape words assigned by $s$ has no state-$a$ visit at any time $t'$ with $0<t'<t$; at time $t$, if $A(x,s)$ is true the run is halted with output $[\mathrm{true}]$, and otherwise it is the seam configuration at $a$ with tape words assigned by $g(x,s)$. Then the loop host in decision mode computes, on every Boolean input $x$, the one-bit word whose bit is true exactly when $A(x,g^{[i]}(s_0(x)))$ holds for some $0\le i\le R(|x|)$, in time $10(T(|x|)+1)(R(|x|)+2)$.
